question: Where can I get a list of airports in the United States, with location, operator and annual passengers, cargo and aircraft movements?

answer.summary: No single file answers it. FAA's NASR 28-day APT file lists 19,434 landing facilities (13,005 airports) with coordinates, owner name and manager name. FAA publishes CY2025 enplanements (516 commercial-service airports, 1,682 in all) and cargo landed weight (155 airports) as Excel. BTS T-100 gives 2024 passengers, departures, freight and mail for 1,279 origin codes on US-carrier domestic flights. FAA TAF gives operations by category to FY2024 for about 3,300 airports. Join on the airport identifier; definitions differ.
main_caveats: Enplanements are passenger boardings, not total passengers. FAA CY and BTS T-100 numbers for the same airport differ: ATL CY2024 52,511,402 (FAA) vs 45,406,031 (BTS 2024); ORD 38,575,693 vs 31,613,389.
BTS T-100 totals cover domestic airports served by US carriers only, by origin code; 37 of 516 FAA commercial-service airports have no matching BTS code and 343 BTS codes are not NASR airport IDs.

TAF operations are fiscal year (Oct-Sep). Towered airports are counted by controllers; at non-FAA facilities operations are estimates. FY2024 is the last actual year in the 2025 TAF; later years are forecasts.
NASR APT.txt is fixed width (230 MB); its annual operations and based-aircraft fields are declared in the layout but empty in all 19,434 records.
Airport, heliport and seaplane base share one file and one counting unit: 13,005 airports among 19,434 facilities. Terminals and runways are separate records.
ADIP and ATADS are form-driven viewers: ADIP is a JavaScript app with a login for airport users, and a scripted ATADS report request returned an empty page.
answer.confidence_reason: NASR, FAA Excel files, BTS T-100 and TAF were downloaded and joined by identifier; ADIP and ATADS were only viewed and the totals definitions across FAA and BTS stay unreconciled.

attributes.note: Airport reference point per facility: 19,434 landing facilities, 13,005 of type airport, with FAA identifier. All 13,005 airport rows carry survey method E (estimated).
NASR gives owner type, owner name (12,887 of 13,005 airports) and a manager name (a person); NTAD gives only the owner type code.
attributes.gap_note: No separate operating organisation field: the manager is a named person and the owner may be a city, authority or private party. Concessionaires and operators other than the owner are not listed.

attributes.note: Enplanements (boardings) per airport: FAA CY2025 for 516 commercial-service airports; BTS T-100 2024 adds passengers per leg. Neither is total arriving plus departing.
attributes.gap_note: Total passengers (arrivals plus departures) were not found in the files tested. Individual airport authority traffic reports were not opened.

attributes.note: FAA CY2025 landed weight in pounds for 155 cargo airports; BTS T-100 2024 freight and mail in pounds for 1,279 origin codes (US carriers, domestic flights).
attributes.gap_note: No file tested gives total cargo (international and belly included) for every airport; FAA covers 155 cargo airports and BTS covers US-carrier domestic flights only.

attributes.note: TAF operations by category (air carrier, air taxi, GA, military; itinerant and local) to FY2024 for about 3,300 airports; BTS departures and arrivals cover T-100 flights only.
attributes.gap_note: ATADS tower counts were not retrieved (report form returned an empty response to scripted requests) and the NASR operations fields are blank in every record.

sources.name: NASR 28 Day Subscription: APT (Airport and landing facility data)
sources.publisher: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), National Flight Data Center
sources.format: ZIP containing APT.txt, fixed-width text (layout in Layout_Data/apt_rf.txt)
sources.license: Unknown (FAA page states none; NTAD copy is a US government work)
sources.summary: FAA NASR airport records: identifier, coordinates, owner type, owner name and manager name for 19,434 landing facilities, refreshed every 28 days.
sources.coverage_note: 13,005 airports among 19,434 facilities; operations fields are blank in this extract; manager is a person.

problems: HEAD request returned 503 while GET returned the file.
Declared operations and based-aircraft fields are empty in every record.

example.example_request: curl -sL -o APT.zip https://nfdc.faa.gov/webContent/28DaySub/2026-10-29/APT.zip; unzip APT.zip APT.txt; read lines starting with APT and slice fixed columns: type 15-27, id 28-31, owner type 184-185, owner name 188-222, manager name 356-390 (positions per Layout_Data/apt_rf.txt)
example.example_result: 19,434 APT records; ORD: AIRPORT, ownership PU, facility use PU, owner CITY OF CHICAGO, effective date 10/29/2026; owner name present on 12,887 of 13,005 airports, manager name on 12,617.

sources.name: Passenger Boarding (Enplanement) and All-Cargo Data for U.S. Airports
sources.publisher: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Office of Airports
sources.format: XLSX (one sheet each); PDF twins; CY2008 onward on the previous-years pages
sources.summary: FAA annual passenger boardings per airport (516 commercial-service, 1,682 in the all-airports file) and cargo landed weight (155 airports) as Excel, CY2025 plus earlier years.
sources.coverage_note: Boardings only; cargo landed weight only for qualifying cargo airports; no coordinates.
caveats: Enplanements are boardings, not total passengers.
Six summary rows sit among the airport rows.

problems: The CY2024 pages show a document date of September 2025 while the page footer says last updated September 2026.

example.example_result: 523 rows: rank 1, ATL, Hartsfield/Jackson Atlanta International, CY25 51,459,786, CY24 52,511,402; rank 3, ORD, CY25 40,680,735, CY24 38,575,693. Cargo file: ANC 26,279,915,354 lb in 2025.

sources.name: T-100 Domestic Market and Segment Data (NTAD table) and TranStats T-100 tables
sources.publisher: Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS), Office of Airline Information
sources.format: ArcGIS REST table (JSON); TranStats tables downloaded through a web form
sources.license: Public domain (NTAD US government work); TranStats terms not read
sources.summary: BTS T-100 totals per origin airport for 2024: enplanements, passengers, departures, arrivals, freight and mail (pounds), as a queryable table of 1,279 rows.
sources.coverage_note: US-carrier domestic flights by origin code; 37 FAA commercial-service airports have no matching code.
caveats: Lower than FAA enplanements at international airports.
Passengers are per leg; enplanements per flight number.
Codes differ from FAA identifiers for 343 rows.

problems: TranStats T-100 downloads go through web forms; the data tables were opened as pages only.
The service has no layer 0; the data are in table id 1.

example.example_result: ORD 2024: enplanements 31613389, passengers 31683551, departures 328086, arrivals 329047, freight 381704912, mail 26670187.

sources.name: Terminal Area Forecast (TAF) 2025 data: AirportsOperations, Enplanements, Airports
sources.format: ZIP (15,670,789 bytes) with five XLSX workbooks: Airports, AirportsOperations, BasedAircraft, Enplanements, Tracon
sources.summary: FAA TAF workbooks with operations by category per airport and fiscal year (history to FY2024) for about 3,300 NPIAS airports, plus enplanements and coordinates.
sources.coverage_note: NPIAS airports only; fiscal years; non-FAA airports are estimates; FY2025 onward is forecast.

problems: The operations workbook has 3,383 identifiers against 3,319 rows in Airports.xlsx; the difference was not explained.

example.example_request: curl -sL -o taf.zip https://taf.faa.gov/Downloads/APO100_TAF_Final_2025.zip; unzip taf.zip; read AirportsOperations.xlsx and keep rows with locid trimmed = 'ORD' and scenario = 0
example.example_result: ORD FY2024 (scenario 0): itn_Ac 627508, itn_at 126342, itn_ga 3743, itn_mil 157, loc_ga 0, loc_mil 0, tot_overs 940. ORD enplanements FY2024: aac 23931683, aat 39, commuter 7456358, us_flag 2953981, frgn_flag 3545993.

local_terms.meaning: FAA page with the cycle downloads, including APT.zip (airport records).
FAA page with yearly Excel files of enplanements and cargo landed weight per airport.
BTS airline traffic tables; the NTAD table gives airport totals by origin.
FAA history and forecast of operations and enplanements by airport and fiscal year.
FAA record holding owner, manager and facility data; viewed in ADIP.
Air Traffic Activity System, the FAA tower operations counts report form.
FAA 3 to 4 character location identifier used to join files (ORD).
National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems; defines the airports in the TAF.

provenance.note: Minutes are researcher estimates. Counts describe documented passes, not publication approval. Missing history or effort is not reconstructed.
